AfterObtained.maps_to: no counterpart on the relic; the +20 Max HP lives in the granting event instead (events/hungry_for_mushrooms.py:34)
AfterObtained.issue: MECHANISM: BigMushroom.cs:24-28 raises Max HP by 20 (MaxHpVar(20m)) in AfterObtained. The sim's relic implements no after_obtained and its docstring justifies that with 'RunState has no run-level AfterObtained dispatch' (big_mushroom.py:19) -- which is FALSE: RunState.add_relic calls relic.after_obtained(self) (run.py:552), and the sibling relic from the very same event, fragrant_mushroom, uses it (events/hungry_for_mushrooms.py:38-40 says so explicitly). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes.py mushroom-hp): run.add_relic('big_mushroom') leaves max_hp at 80, while run.add_relic('fragrant_mushroom') correctly drops hp 80 -> 65 through its own after_obtained. The event path happens to be whole (max_hp 80 -> 100) because the event re-applies the +20 itself, so ordinary play is unaffected -- but the conformance runner grants relics by id straight through add_relic (conformance/runner.py:465, 698, 751) when it resyncs the player's relics against the save, and that path silently loses 20 Max HP. Since DETECTOR 3 asserts player HP and max HP at act boundaries, this surfaces as a parity failure on any seed whose player took Big Mushroom. The same misplacement also defeats Relic.undo_after_obtained (relics/base.py:143-150), which exists precisely so a swapped-out max-HP relic unwinds its bonus: Big Mushroom's +20 is not the relic's to unwind, so a runner swap leaves it behind.

AfterRoomEntered.rationale: BigMushroom.cs:30-34 calls Grow(), whose entire body is `NCombatRoom.Instance?.GetCreatureNode(Owner.Creature)?.ScaleTo(1.5f, 0.0)` (lines 49-52) -- it scales the player's sprite. Pure presentation; the sim has no scene graph. Named rather than waived generically because AfterRoomEntered IS a modelled hook in the sim (Relic.after_room_entered, relics/base.py:194), so its absence here could otherwise look like an oversight.

ModifyHandDraw.rationale: BigMushroom.cs:36-47 subtracts CardsVar(2).IntValue from the draw on TurnNumber == 1 for its owner; big_mushroom.py:30-31 subtracts DRAW_REDUCTION = 2 on `self.turn == 1`. Note C# spells this one `!= 1` where its batch siblings spell theirs `> 1` or `<= 1` -- the sim's `== 1` matches the actual predicate, not the sibling idiom. Same dispatcher and same base-5 draw as relic/bag_of_preparation (player.py:171, turn_structure step 20); the two relics compose additively and order-independently, which bag_of_preparation's guard N2 records.

guards.rationale: The value is right wherever it lives; only its LOCATION is the gap above. No ascension branch in the file. Recorded so a fix that moves the +20 onto the relic does not also have to re-derive the number -- and so that whoever moves it remembers to delete the event's copy, or the event path will grant 40.

guards.what: N2: CardsVar(2) is read with IntValue on the draw path (BigMushroom.cs:46) while relic/bag_of_preparation reads its CardsVar with BaseValue (BagOfPreparation.cs:24)
guards.rationale: Both resolve to 2 with no ascension branch declared, so the inconsistency is cosmetic in the source and neither sim port is wrong. Recorded because the contract pins numeric constants to the non-ascension branch and a reader comparing the two files should not conclude one of them is reading the wrong field.
